Priyom / Marissa — draft responses below. I focused on the requested evidence and kept the wording conservative for audits. Attachments: vnet-slicing-diagram-20261001.pdf (diagram), private-isolation-matrix-20261002.xlsx (control matrix).

High-level summary (to include on cover page):
- Redwood Private supports logical virtual network slicing: each tenant is provisioned into an isolated overlay (VRF/segment) with control-plane components logically separated and authenticated via mutual TLS. Data plane traffic is permitted only according to route tables and firewall policies attached to the tenant slice.
- Administrative access to control-plane services is restricted using role-based access controls and guarded by jump hosts + bastion in a dedicated management VPC. Audit logs for both control and data plane are delivered to the customer's logging endpoint or a customer-designated S3-compatible bucket; we provide hash-signed delivery receipts.

Controls matrix (excerpt):
- Per-slice firewalling: stateful rules applied at the tenant boundary (implemented by virtual firewall instances / NSG equivalent).
- Route isolation: tenants get dedicated route tables and VRFs; inter-VRF leaking is disabled by default.
- KMS boundaries: customers may bring their own KMS keys; keys are not shared across tenants.
- Egress controls: egress NAT gateways are dedicated per-slice when requested; otherwise egress passes through a controlled transit VPC with enforced egress rules.

Known limitations / trade-offs:
- Shared physical network: on colocation or cloud-hosted Private deployments we rely on the cloud provider's switching fabric for packet forwarding; we mitigate risk with strong logical controls but cannot guarantee hardware-level isolation.
- Cross-tenant telemetry: aggregated telemetry pipelines (metrics) are aggregated but not materially readable per-tenant; sensitive log streams are delivered directly to the customer's secure endpoint.

Next steps: Marissa to finalize diagram and I will produce a 1-page auditor-friendly blurb. Priyom to assemble and send.

Karthik
